record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.original_question: How can ultra-dense cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) implement low-complexity interference-suppression precoding and combining that cancels only the most significant intra-access-point (intra-AP) and inter-access-point (inter-AP) interference, avoids large pseudo-inverse computations, limits fronthaul overhead, and still approaches the performance of network-wide zero forcing or minimum mean-square error (MMSE)-style processing?

evidence.quote: 1) Low-complexity processing: When designing interference-suppression-based precoding and combining schemes, the complexity of implementing the beamforming vectors mainly lies in the computation of the pseudo-inverse matrix, hence on its size.
In CF-MMIMO, due to the distributed network topology, the dynamic range of the interference from/to different APs may be large.
These are fully distributed precoding schemes that provide an adaptable trade-off between interference cancellation and boosting of the desired signal, with no additional fronthaul overhead.

Such a joint MR transmission and ZF (JMRZF) precoding scheme converges to the performance of network-wide ZF as the number of APs included in the ZF set grows, at the expense of an increased computational complexity and fronthaul overhead.

artifact.status_search_result: Partial solutions exist: distributed schemes such as local partial zero-forcing (PZF), local protective partial ZF (PPZF), full-pilot ZF, and joint MR–ZF (JMRZF) precoding have been proposed and analyzed, providing adjustable trade-offs between interference cancellation, complexity, and fronthaul overhead, with convergence to network-wide ZF as the local ZF set grows. However, a fully satisfactory low-complexity scheme that selectively cancels only the most significant intra- and inter-AP interference, avoids large pseudo-inverses, keeps fronthaul bounded, and provably approaches network-wide ZF/MMSE in ultra-dense CF-MMIMO remains an active research problem.

status_evidence.title: Local Partial Zero-Forcing Precoding for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
status_evidence.snippet: Two distributed precoding schemes called local partial zero-forcing (PZF) and local protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) … provide an adaptable trade-off between interference cancellation and boosting of the desired signal, with no additional fronthaul overhead.
status_evidence.claim: Partial low-complexity distributed ZF-type precoders exist and address part of the problem.

status_evidence.title: Local Partial Zero-Forcing Combining for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
status_evidence.snippet: Partial zero-forcing combining significantly reduces intra-group interference at reduced complexity compared to network-wide combiners.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works treat low-complexity intra-/inter-AP interference suppression as ongoing research.
